title: Upgrade orchestration safety matrix and canary-sim runbook
creator: Aisha Thompson
description: Create a reproducible safety matrix and an executable runbook for release orchestration that standardizes canary simulations, percent-ramp profiles, feature-flag gating, and automated rollback conditions across LTS and patch channels. This ticket produces: 1) a Safety Matrix doc mapping metrics -> thresholds -> severity, 2) a Canary-Sim harness (lightweight simulator) that predicts SLO and error behavior for proposed ramps, and 3) an operational runbook with explicit playbook steps for automated and manual rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Safety Matrix published in Confluence with metric owners and alert thresholds
Canary-Sim tool runs deterministic simulations for a given traffic profile and outputs pass/fail and confidence bands
Runbook contains step-by-step automated ramp commands, manual override checklist, and rollback triggers
PR created to wire automation into CI/CD (release-orch repo) and smoke tests added
Two rehearsal runs executed in staging that match simulation predictions within allowed error margin
implementation_notes: Define canonical metric set: p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, error_rate, model_inference_timeout, cpu_utilization, kv_cache_hit_rate
Safety Matrix assigns severity levels and per-channel tolerances (LTS vs patch vs ephemeral) with explicit degradation windows
Canary-Sim accepts input: baseline distribution, ramp schedule, injected fault scenarios, and returns simulated traces and SLO breach probability
Implement canary orchestration step in release-orch with flags: --profile=canary-slope, --max-step=10, --hold=10m
Add API hooks for "dry-run" to test runbook without changing traffic
Create unit tests for Sim harness and e2e smoke test for ramping workflow
ramp_plan: Stage: canary-quick: 0% -> 1% over 5m, hold 15m, evaluate metrics
Stage: canary-slope: 1% -> 10% linear over 60m, automated checks every 5m
Stage: scale-to-medium: 10% -> 40% over 2h with adaptive pauses if any metric sees a 2x delta from baseline
Stage: full-traffic: 40% -> 100% in customer-batch windows with final verification tasks
Feature-flag gating: enable model variant under feature flag 'model.v2.canary' during canary stages only
rollback_conditions: Absolute: error_rate > 0.5% for two consecutive evaluation windows (5m each)
Relative: p95_latency increases > 2x baseline sustained for >15m
Resource: GPU memory pressure > 85% for >10m or unexpected OOM events
Safety net: Canary-Sim predicted breach probability > 60% for proposed next step
Manual: on-call or SRE can trigger 'immediate rollback' with documented pager steps
monitoring_queries: Synthetic: canary-invoker healthcheck success rate from canary agents
Logs: sample error signatures and model traceback aggregated by fingerprint

risks: Simulation mismatch risk: sampling biases in Canary-Sim leading to optimistic predictions
Operational complexity: too many manual steps in runbook increases human error during critical windows
Cross-channel drift: LTS tolerances being too strict can block urgent patches; need separate fast-path rules
False positives: overly aggressive auto-rollback could cause unnecessary reverts and customer churn
notes: Decision: separate LTS and patch channel policies; LTS requires two independent metric breaches before auto-rollback, patch channel can use single metric with human approval
